questions.question: A continuous loss $X$ has density $f_\theta$ and is right-censored at known cap $c$: a capped record means only $X\ge c$. Which likelihood contribution is valid for every continuous loss model under non-informative censoring?
A continuous loss sample contains exact records and records giving only $X_i\ge c_i$ at known caps $c_i$. Should the capped policies be included in the likelihood?
options: Yes; each retained record supplies tail information.
No; only exact losses are observations.
Yes; each should be recorded as a zero ground-up loss.
No; their loss amounts are smaller than the caps.

questions.question: A continuous loss has density $f_\theta$ and is right-censored at a known cap. An exported record displays amount 20, but its cap and exact/censored indicator are omitted. What information is needed to select its general likelihood contribution?
options: No extra information: use $f_\theta(20)$ for every such record.
No extra information: use $\mathbb{P}_\theta(X\ge20)$ for every such record.
Retain its cap or exact/censored status.

questions.question: The usual right-censoring contribution uses a loss density below the cap and a survivor probability at the cap. Why must censoring be non-informative for this observation model?
options: It guarantees the loss density is constant.
Loss-dependent censoring can change the observed law.
It makes every censored loss equal its cap.
It guarantees that no censored records occur.

questions.question: A loss distribution has positive probability mass at cap $c$. A censored record states $X\ge c$, while survivor $\bar F(c)=\mathbb{P}(X>c)$ is strict. Which formula gives its likelihood contribution for every such loss law?
Independent exponential losses have unknown rate $\lambda>0$. The data contain exact losses 20 and 30 and one censored record at cap 100. What is the rate MLE?
A continuous exponential loss has rate $\lambda=0.02$. A record states only that the loss reaches a known cap of 50. What is its likelihood contribution?
Independent exponential losses have rate $\lambda>0$. One exact observation is 10 below its cap, and a second is censored at 40. Which joint likelihood formula is valid for every positive rate?
An exponential loss of rate $\lambda>0$ is censored at known cap $c>0$. Which log-likelihood expression is valid for every positive rate and cap?
A policy has a right-censored loss record at cap 100: the only observation is $X\ge100$. Which exact ground-up amount can be recovered from that record alone?
options: No single exact amount is identified.

questions.question: For independent exponential losses of rate $\lambda>0$, there are $n$ retained records and $r>0$ exact losses; the remainder are censored. Let $T\in(0,\infty)$ be the sum of exact losses and censored caps. Why is the rate estimator $r/T$, rather than $n/T$?
options: Only exact observations contribute to the exposure sum.
Only exact observations supply the log-rate terms.
Censored observations have probability independent of the rate.
Exact observations each represent the entire sample.

questions.question: Independent exponential losses of rate $\lambda>0$ are all right-censored at positive caps summing to $T>0$. The likelihood is $\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda T}$. What maximisation conclusion follows?
options: The likelihood is constant over positive rates.
Its supremum is approached as the rate decreases to zero.
A positive maximum occurs as the rate tends to infinity.

questions.question: An exponential loss of fixed rate $\lambda>0$ stays censored while its known cap changes from $c_1$ to $c_2>c_1>0$. Which log-likelihood change formula is valid for every positive rate?
options: It stays unchanged because both values are caps.

questions.question: Independent exponential losses have common rate $\lambda\in[0.02,0.1]$. There are two exact records and three non-informatively censored records, with exact amounts and censored caps totalling 200. What is the constrained rate MLE?

Independent exponential loss records share rate $\lambda>0$. Dataset A has exact losses 10,20 and one censored cap 60. Dataset B has exact losses 5,25 and censored caps 20,40. Which comparison of their likelihoods holds for every positive rate?
An exponential loss sample of unknown rate $\lambda>0$ contains four exact positive observations with sum 80 and no censored records. What does the right-censoring rate formula reduce to?
A continuous ground-up loss $X$ is recorded as $Z=\min(X,c)$ at a fixed cap $c>0$, with $\mathbb{P}(X\ge c)>0$. Why can the recorded distribution have positive probability at exactly $c$?
options: The ground-up law must already have an atom at the cap.
All losses at or above the cap map to that recorded value.
The exact-loss density becomes an exact-point probability.
The selected population excludes all losses above the cap.

questions.question: A continuous loss $X>0$ is hidden at cap $C=X/2$, so every record is censored and the observed cap itself reveals $X=2C$. Would treating $C$ as non-informative and using only a survivor factor describe all recorded information?
options: Yes; every censored record always uses only a survivor factor.
Yes; positive caps imply censoring is independent of loss.
No; a censored record must have zero probability.
No; the cap and loss are linked by the observation mechanism.

questions.question: Two right-censored samples consist of mutually independent exponential losses sharing one rate $\lambda>0$. Sample A has 1 exact record and total exposure 10; B has 3 exact records and total exposure 90, where exposure sums exact amounts and censored caps. What is the pooled rate MLE?

Two independent exponential-loss observations share unknown rate $\lambda>0$ and realise 20 and 45. Under a common cap 30, only 20 is exact; under a common cap 60, both are exact. Which pair gives their rate MLEs under caps 30 and 60 respectively?
